PullRequest.Title: chat: support named and prompted Agent Host forks
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #341229

## Summary

Add named and prompted forks to Agent Host chats in the editor and Agents windows:

- `/fork` keeps its immediate fork behavior.
- `/fork <title>` creates a fork with the specified initial title.
- `/fork prompt <prompt>` creates a fork and sends the prompt with attached context. VS Code's naming strategy can use the source title and new prompt.

The three completion entries have distinct localized descriptions. The title/prompt templates insert without submitting, show argument hints, and highlight the complete command prefix without adding command-token editing side effects.

Following review of the [AHP companion PR](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/526), all fork variants use the existing fork capability. Optional titles and the existing `initialMessage` need no additional capability. Older hosts may ignore the new title field.

Initial-message failures appear as ordinary errors in the created chat, rather than a special creation RPC error. Admission-rejected initial messages survive reload; ordinary rejected turns retain their existing persistence behavior. Unknown transport/navigation outcomes show the underlying error and offer target inspection without automatically resending. Source-turn selection, model/agent inheritance, attachment handling, and source-owned draft cleanup remain intact.

The title-restoration repair drains the owning session's pending metadata and catalog writes before idle release. A controlled compatibility-storage regression reproduced a saved rename being replaced by the older cached title during reopening. The repair preserves title precedence and error propagation, scopes both active and passive catalog waits to the owning session, and leaves the existing restart E2E expectations unchanged.

## How to test

In both window types, open an Agent Host conversation with at least one completed turn:

1. Accept `/fork` and verify it forks immediately.
2. Accept `/fork <title>`, enter a title, and submit. Verify the fork starts with that title.
3. Accept `/fork prompt <prompt>`. Verify `/fork prompt` is command-colored and the argument hint is separate. Enter a prompt, attach context, and submit; verify one new request in the fork with inherited history.
4. Type/delete arguments and edit the prefix; verify hints and normal editing remain correct.
5. Verify a rejected initial message appears as an errored turn in the new chat; after reload it is still visible, with no automatic resend.
6. Rename a titled peer chat, switch away and reopen it, then restart the host. Verify the renamed title is retained in both the chat and session catalog.

## Draft notes

- Companion protocol PR: https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/526. The title-loss repair adds no protocol fields or schema changes.
- Cross-platform CI is still required, particularly the Windows/Electron scenario that originally failed. Local macOS passes are not a Windows-success claim.
- Cross-platform Azure validation has not run; local Azure CLI authentication is unavailable.
- A local replay attempt and lint invocation were blocked before execution by the previously observed shared Node/npm executable-permission issue. Both succeeded after restoring owner-execute permission.
- Earlier live Agents Window validation covered hints, prefix coloring, and editing. This repair and main merge were validated with automated tests, not a new live UI run.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added completion installs this local hint, the added content-change listener invokes the check on every edit, and the added tests establish that the hint remains alive while argument text is present. The exact cost depends on prompt length, but the full-range allocation and edit-path reachability are explicit.
Findings.PerformanceResource: UI-thread string copying and scanning allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(L) work and allocation per edit for prompt length L; O(L^2) cumulative copying across incremental typing, or O(E×L) for E edits to a long pasted prompt
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased input latency and CPU/GC pressure while editing long fork prompts
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, `/fork` was an immediate command and this local `/fork prompt` hint state and its per-edit full-suffix read did not exist on that workflow.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After accepting the new `/fork prompt <prompt>` completion, every subsequent prompt edit synchronously copies and scans the entire text after the command prefix to decide whether the argument hint should be visible.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The diff adds a persistent local command hint and, at RIGHT line 216, materializes `model.getValueInRange(afterRange)` from the `/fork prompt` prefix through the end of the input. The newly added model-content listener calls `update()` for every edit, and the new test `restores a local hint after deleting an argument...` confirms the hint remains installed while an argument is present.
Findings.Title: Avoid copying the full fork prompt on every edit
Findings.Impact: Editing a long pasted `/fork prompt` can incur input lag and GC churn: every keystroke or deletion allocates a new string proportional to the full prompt length. Typing a prompt incrementally performs cumulative quadratic character copying.
Findings.Evidence: `rebindEditor()` calls `update()` on every `onDidChangeModelContent`; `getLocalHintDecoration()` constructs an `afterRange` ending at `getFullModelRange()` and line 216 calls `getValueInRange` before merely checking `startsWith(' ')` and equality with one space. Because `localHint` is not cleared when additional argument text follows that space, this repeats for every character/edit. The `/fork prompt` completion at `chatSlashCommands.ts:233` is the new trigger.
Findings.Recommendation: Avoid reading the full suffix. Check the character immediately after the prefix and compare model positions/length to determine whether exactly one trailing space remains (for example with line/position metadata or a length query), so each edit stays constant or logarithmic without allocating the prompt.

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing and editing the new `/fork prompt` completion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Slash suggestions await the capability lookup before displaying results. For an active widget this is an in-memory hit. Once a title/prompt completion is accepted, the local hint update runs synchronously on every editor content change.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Characters in the `/fork prompt` argument and number of subsequent edits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Completion requests are cancellation-aware; cold session resolution is coalesced per resource. Editor hint updates are serialized synchronously on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The active chat session is normally already present in `ChatSessionsService._sessions`, so the new fork-capability lookup is a warm map hit. Cold resolutions are coalesced in `_pendingSessionResolutions`, and cancellation removes the waiter; failures are not negatively cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added content listener reaches a full-range `getValueInRange` on every edit, and tests establish that the hint remains alive while argument text is present.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical short prompts make the added copy small; the exact jank threshold depends on prompt length and edit rate. Long pasted prompts followed by edits are realistic, but no timing measurement is available.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the changed local-hint path performs O(prompt length) UI-thread allocation per edit, yielding cumulative quadratic copying during incremental typing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating a bare or named Agent Host fork
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user waits for one `createChat` protocol request, provider chat creation, host catalog persistence/publication, and target opening. A supplied title adds title metadata persistence but no additional protocol round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the provider-backed fork and publish it in the host catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One AHP `createChat` request per non-coalesced fork.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Bare forks already issued one create-chat request; named forks add a field to that same request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the target chat is opened.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create backing chat and persist peer catalog metadata; named forks also persist the explicit title.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider chat creation plus bounded catalog/title persistence per fork.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Bare forks already created and persisted a peer chat; the diff adds title values without increasing fork-level call cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider creation and catalog publication are on the fork critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation per user fork; inherited turn count affects existing fork-history preparation but is not multiplied by the new title option.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fork creation is serialized by session catalog mutation sequencing on the host. Duplicate contributed forks with the same identity are coalesced in `pendingForks`; different titles/prompts remain independent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The session/chat catalogs and selected model/agent are read from provider caches; chat publication waits on observable state rather than polling. No new unbounded cache is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call flow and sequencing are explicit and tests verify a single creation/publication.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider creation and storage latency vary by agent and local/remote host, but the diff does not multiply calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression: named forks reuse the existing single creation boundary and add bounded metadata.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating a fork and sending its initial prompt with attachments
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A prompt fork snapshots variables, reconciles working directory and active client state, sends one create-chat request, creates/publishes the peer, rewrites attached resources, admits and dispatches the initial turn, then opens the target. The provider response itself is off the create RPC critical path after turn dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize launch context and submitting client identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one working-directory reconciliation and one active-client claim per prompt fork; warm state can make these no-ops.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Bare forks did not prepare a first message; an equivalent later ordinary send performed the same preparation separately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One AHP `createChat` request carrying the fork source, title, and initial message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fork creation and a subsequent user send were separate operations; the new variant combines them into one request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must return before navigation completes; the host publishes the target before admitting the turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/rewrite resource attachments through the submitting client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for simple/embedded attachments; otherwise one client resource read per attached resource, concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-attachment reads occurred on a later ordinary send; the diff moves them into the composed fork request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Attachment rewriting completes before the initial turn is admitted and before create-chat returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the initial model/agent turn in the created fork.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider turn dispatch after successful admission.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Users had to send a separate first turn after creating a fork.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dispatch is awaited only through host-side outgoing-turn preparation, not through model response completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Inherited turns, attached resource count/bytes, and number of distinct concurrent prompt forks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One create request per non-coalesced prompt identity. Host catalog mutation is sequenced per session. Attached resource rewrites use `Promise.all`, so cardinality equals distinct attached resources with no shared limiter, but this matches the ordinary send path and is bounded by the composer attachment set.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Working-directory and active-client reconcilers retain session state and avoid redundant claims when already current. Target session models are retained briefly after hydration to avoid immediate reload. No automatic retry/resend occurs on unknown outcomes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the combined path, one-request semantics, attachment fan-out, and per-session sequencing are explicit in code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Attachment count/size and remote-host latency vary; no evidence shows increased effective cardinality versus the equivalent fork-then-send workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the expensive boundaries are required once for the new composed operation and do not multiply equivalent fork-plus-send work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automatic naming and lifecycle of prompt-bearing forks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Utility title generation may issue one existing utility-model request; active-agent/deferred strategies keep naming work off chat creation except for bounded context construction and persistence.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Generate an automatic title from bounded inherited and new-prompt context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one utility-model title request for a prompt fork under the utility strategy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Bare forks already scheduled one utility title request; the diff enriches its bounded input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Scheduled asynchronously and does not block fork creation or initial turn dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist bounded source-title and initial-prompt context for deferred naming.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded metadata writes per deferred title seed/context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Deferred fork seeds stored title and turn index without the extra bounded context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget relative to user interaction; release drains pending writes before evicting state.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of resident prompt-fork chats and bounded title-context size (up to the configured context budget).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Title generation uses existing per-key cancellation/replacement; no new aggregate burst was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fork title context is truncated to bounded strings and removed on refinement, rename, instruction consumption, session eviction, or disposal. Deferred seeds are persisted/restored per chat.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for lifecycle and bounds; lower for material memory impact under realistic chat counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Admission-rejected active-agent forks can retain bounded context until retry or session teardown, but realistic retained volume was not sufficient for a high-confidence user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No report: context is individually bounded and has session/chat cleanup; observed worst-case accumulation did not establish material impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Idle release or deletion while title/catalog writes are pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new waits run during idle release/deletion, after interactive subscribers are gone. They are not on chat input, rendering, or active turn response paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Drain peer metadata and background catalog writes before releasing session data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: All outstanding metadata, catalog, and session-database writes for the one releasing session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Release waited only on the session database and could race peer/catalog writes; global synchronization elsewhere could wait on unrelated sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delays background eviction/deletion only; it preserves write ordering before state is discarded.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Outstanding writes for the releasing session, not total writes across all sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Writes remain serialized per session; the drain waits for that session's current and newly queued writes and uses settled waits where failures are reported elsewhere.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pending peer metadata/catalog writes are tracked by owning session, preventing unrelated sessions from extending a release drain.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call site is teardown/release and the tracked writes are session-filtered.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A slow or stuck write can extend resident lifetime, but session scoping removes cross-session fan-out and no interactive critical path is blocked.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: the added wait is background cleanup synchronization and is narrowed to the owning session.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all changed files. Submitted one medium synchronous UI/input finding for full-prompt copying on each `/fork prompt` edit. Fork transport, attachment, persistence, cache/coalescing, title lifecycle, and release-drain scenarios were traced without another high-confidence regression.
